references.text: Jesus directly confirms the connection between God's glory and faith that He will be glorified, a central theme in verse 4 where the sickness is for God's glory.
Jesus speaks of how "the Son of Man shall be glorified" through His death, which mirrors the statement in verse 4 that the Son's glory will be revealed through suffering.
In His solemn prayer, Jesus asks the Father to glorify the Son's name, a direct fulfillment of the theme in verse 4 that the Son's glory will be revealed.
Jesus explains that a blind man's suffering is not due to sin, but so that God's works may be displayed in him, paralleling how Lazarus's sickness is for God's glory.
Jesus proclaims that "the Son of Man has been glorified" and that God will be glorified in Him, linking back to the statement in verse 4 that the Son's glory will be revealed through this event.
